title: The canonical punctured comparison Y→r⁻¹(U) is an isomorphism.
statement: Let A be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], U an open of Spec A consisting exactly of the points other than its closed point [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], q:Y→U and s:E→Spec C finite morphisms [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], where C is the maximal-ideal completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let D be an overlap identification and let B, F, r and the canonical comparisons be the explicit matching-sections constructions [def-sbc-punctured-completion-matching-sections]. The canonical punctured comparison Y→r⁻¹(U) is an isomorphism. This asserts no finiteness or other comparison property of the candidate.

proof.text: For any point x of the target of D.puncturedMap, choose a principal open D(f) of Spec A contained in U and containing its image. Such an open exists by the principal-open basis. Its preimage V in U is affine: the open immersion U→Spec A identifies V with D(f). The structural morphism of the explicit affine model is affine, and so is its restriction r to U. Thus W=r⁻¹(V) is affine and contains x.

The identity D.puncturedMap_over identifies the inverse image of W under D.puncturedMap with q⁻¹(V). Since q is finite, this inverse image is affine. Apply the principal-open section comparison to obtain bijectivity of the appTop ring map of D.puncturedMap restricted to W.

A bijective morphism of commutative rings is an isomorphism. For a morphism between affine schemes, an isomorphism on global sections implies it is an isomorphism, by the Spec–Γ equivalence (Mathlib HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine for isomorphisms). Thus each restriction to W is an isomorphism. Apply Mathlib IsZariskiLocalAtTarget.of_forall_exists_morphismRestrict for isomorphisms. This also handles an empty target, because the pointwise condition is vacuous.
